name: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
summary: A prone shoulder raise performed on an incline bench to target the lower trapezius and lateral deltoids through the scapular plane.

setup: Set an adjustable bench to a 30- to 45-degree incline.
Straddle the bench and lie prone with your chest fully supported by the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight down toward the floor, palms facing inward and thumbs pointed slightly upward.
steps: Maintain a soft bend in the elbows and brace your torso against the pad.
Raise both arms diagonally outward at roughly a 30- to 45-degree angle from your torso to form a 'Y' shape.
Continue raising until your upper arms align roughly with your torso and ears.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize lower trapezius contraction.
Lower the dumbbells smoothly back to the starting hanging position under full control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells into the Y position, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Lead with your shoulder blades rotating up, not your traps shrugging to your ears

common_faults.correction: Focus on depressing and upwardly rotating the scapulae rather than using the upper traps to heave the weight.

common_faults.fault: Using body momentum or hyperextending the lower back off the pad.
common_faults.correction: Keep your sternum pinned to the bench pad throughout the entire movement; reduce the dumbbell weight if necessary.

common_faults.fault: Raising arms purely to the side or purely to the front.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a diagonal path roughly midway between a lateral raise and a front raise (in the scapular plane).

precautions: Use light weights; this movement isolates relatively small scapular and shoulder muscles.
